content.title: Toyota Recalls 550,007 Highlander SUVs Over Seat Backs That May Fail To Lock
content.text: The world's largest automaker is recalling a great deal of Highlander sport utility vehicles. According to the recall documentation uploaded on the NHTSA's website, the second-row seat backs of an estimated 550,007 vehicles may fail to lock into position during seat back adjustment. Suspect production dates range from March 31, 2021, for the 2021 model year through November 10, 2023, for the 2024 model year. Both internal combustion and hybrid models are being recalled by Toyota Motor North America. The root cause behind the recall condition is a design change made by the supplier. Toyota Boshoku Indiana is the supplier listed in the recall documentation. The design change resulted in recliner teeth that may not fully engage during adjustment, a condition that greatly increases the risk of injury in the event of a crash. Toyota became aware of the reported condition back in October 2023, during a routine inspection. The subject vehicle was found to skip the first locking position during seat back adjustment. Shortly thereafter, the plant and the supplier both initiated stricter inspection activities to identify second-row seats with this issue. Toyota wasn't made aware of the design change to the guide and ratchet within the recliner assembly, which its supplier introduced back in April 2021. During replication tests, five of 20 seats contained a seat back that failed to remain in the locked position. Photo: Toyota To date, Toyota Motor North America has received 10 field reports and 18 warranty claims related to the recall condition. All known customers will be notified by first-class mail between April 20, 2026, and May 4, 2026. Dealers have already been instructed to replace the return springs in the recliner assemblies. The parts and labor come free of charge. In the meantime, customers may run the 17-character VINs of their Highlander vehicles on the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration's website to find out if their SUVs are being recalled. VINs kick off with 5 because the Highlander is made in the United States. In the fifth position, you will find either A for the 2.5-liter hybrid powertrain or K for the 2.4-liter turbo gasser. The sixth position is more of the same, namely R for the hybrid or 3 for the gas-only specification. 56,208 examples of the Highlander were sold in the US last year, down 37.3 percent from 2024. By comparison, the roomier Grand Highlander moved 136,801 and 71,721 units, respectively. One of the segment's most popular three-row crossovers, the Highlander went fully electric for its fifth generation. Coming to dealers for the 2027 model year in the latter part of 2026, the all-new Highlander is available with either front-wheel drive or a dual-motor option. Revealed in February 2026, the redesigned Highlander is estimated with up to 320 miles (515 kilometers) of range on a full charge. Liked the article?
